questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: interesting culture in Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The system were pretty bad. There were little to non information regarding info and lessons

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i recieved a mail with some infomation regarding where to pick up my student ID

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with a friend i knew already, and she were the one finding housing. She found it through facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can take a long time with public transport. we had almost 1 hour each way to the university. But this was also because I ended up with other courses than first anticipated.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 3/5 of my pre approved courses were not avaiable when I arrived. So i was forces to have some courses that really didnt make to much sense.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were alot of steps, which could be a little confusing at times

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Daniel Stokke were helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. as said before 2/5 of the courses were not taut in Milano, but rather in Copenhagen. Therefore i had to chose something else. Another course were scheduled at the same time of the week, so I had to chose another one there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about the courses, because its out of your hands. The italian way is more laid back, so dont stress.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Im studying geography, but had a master level course in law, one in economics and 2 in geology. This was at times a pretty tough task.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no hands on. Only lectures. The english level of some professors was really bad, and actually so hard to understand, that you didnt catch the knowledge.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
-gender justice
-food chain in the global market
-waste management
-georessources
-geological evolution of a habitable planet

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
-geological evolution of a habitable planet
even tho its not completely a geography course, it is really relevant. We had to argue about the relevance of the course, but in the end it got accepted. The professor speak english well and the course is well structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The italian culture eats out way more often than in denmark. So you eat out and drink out way more. It is cheaper, but you still spent more money than you would do if you did your groceries yourself.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing were expensive. it was hard to find anything, and we were forces to pick a place that were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I received a mail 3 month into the semester from my tutor saying they were ready to welcome me. At that time it didnt matter.
Fitness were expensive. hard to find sport (i tried to find a place to play football, but coulndt find any)
the university did not inform about social events like parties or gatherings.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: none i could get information about. much of the info was in italien, and not very suitable for international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: none that the university arranged. A had a trip to the Dolomites and to Firenze. Both of these were amazing and is highly recomended.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: take part in the football culture on the stadium. there are 2 top class teams in Milan, and watching these in the stadium is enjoyable. Local cafees and bars are really cosy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: medium level

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: i did not socialize with any locals. I had some connection with other international students. but the italian locals did not feel very welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: there are dogs everywhere. people are super unaware on the pavements and in public transport. they walk really slow and stop and dont seem to be aware of their surroundings

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the cafee life. coffee is cheap and the culture of drinking coffee and eat crossaint is much more appreciated for me than in denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be more aware of telling or helping the students when they stress about courses and lack of information.
For geographical students, there are not many suitable courses. so if you can be large with what they can pick.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting some really nice exchangestudents. and going on trips. Italy have great opportunities to see culture and nature, so dont miss that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: difficulties regarding information and courses. Also all my courses were exceptionally bad at informing about the exams. time, place, expectations, formation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
